threads.body: Metric observations are keyed by their emitted name, but the model now also contains refinement IDs as keys. A metric emitted as `demo.skill.duration` therefore gets recorded as refinement coverage even though that refinement declares the metric name `demo.duration`, without any explicit refinement selection. Check the definition's actual name before retaining the observation so a metric name that merely matches a refinement ID is not counted.

replies.body: The `definition.get("name", name) != name` guard in 25b52c33 fixes this. The underlying cause is that `model["metrics"]` now mixes refinement ids in with metric names, so every consumer has to know to skip them (`signal_coverage` in the report gets away with it only because the data never contains those keys). Since base metrics already carry their refinements under `refinements`, could the template drop the separate refinement entries from `metrics`, or move them to their own map? The guard would then be unnecessary. Happy either way; if you keep it, a short comment on the guard explaining why would help.
Metrics are keyed by name now, so the guard is gone.

threads.body: Minor and not reachable with today's data, since no signal is reported by more than one runner. Still, this widens the conflict check: two runners whose pins agree on a signal's base attributes but differ in its refinements would now throw "Conflicting declarations", and the whole page fails to render. Comparing `declared?.attributes` here as before, and merging refinements only for display, would keep the check about real declaration conflicts.

replies.body: The conflict check compares base attributes again.

threads.body: `LEVELS` is documented as "Requirement levels from the registry", but `refinement` records where an attribute came from, not a level the registry assigns. Adding it here means `rank()`, `levelLegend()` and the signals "all levels" filter all treat it as a level. That works today, but anything later that maps `LEVELS` to registry semantics will pick it up silently. Would it be cleaner to keep the real level and carry a separate `refinementAttributes` set on the signal entry? Not blocking if you'd rather keep it simple.

replies.body: `refinementAttributes` is separate now, and `LEVELS` only has registry levels.

threads.body: This reuses the colour of `recommended_conditional`, so on a signal that has both groups the legend and heatmap header show two identical swatches. Could the unscored group get its own token (or a muted/neutral one, since it isn't scored)?

threads.body: `refinementAttributes` merges declarations from every runner, so if only runner B declares `vendor.response` in a refinement, runner A's page also treats an emitted `vendor.response` as declared and removes it from “Not in the registry.” Derive this set from `data.report.registry[found.runner]` so the target is compared against its own registry, while keeping the union for the comparison heatmap.
